outcome: Proportion of women attending >= 5 antenatal visits
Epidural analgesia in the first stage of labour
Normal birth (term, spontaneous onset, vertex, spontaneous vaginal birth, no epidural, no episiotomy)
cohort: The study included 1259 women from a refugee background (625 receiving Refugee Midwifery Group Practice care and 634 receiving standard care) who gave birth at a large tertiary hospital in Australia.
finding: Women who received Refugee Midwifery Group Practice care were more likely to have spontaneous onset of labour and normal birth, and less likely to use epidural analgesia and have a preterm baby.
mod_finding: Women receiving Refugee Midwifery Group Practice care were more likely to have a normal birth (defined as term, spontaneous onset, vertex, spontaneous vaginal birth, no epidural, no episiotomy) and less likely to use epidural analgesia.
